nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: High-altitude sun powers the sparse plants of the dune field and the grasslands around it.

nodes.name: Snowmelt and Medano Creek
nodes.wiki: Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve
nodes.desc: Mountain snowmelt feeds Medano Creek and the water table. Wikipedia says peak creek flow is usually late May to early June.

nodes.name: Moist dune sand
nodes.desc: Wikipedia says moist sand just under the surface lets dune plants, the tiger beetle and Ord's kangaroo rat survive here.

nodes.name: Summer rain
nodes.desc: Rain wets the sand sheet and shrublands and helps seeds sprout.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and detritus feeders break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the sand.

nodes.name: Pinyon pine
nodes.desc: A small pine of the drier slopes, listed by Wikipedia among the park's trees. Its large seeds are a food for birds and rodents.

nodes.name: Rubber rabbitbrush
nodes.desc: A hardy shrub of the sandy shrublands around the dunes that deer can browse.

nodes.name: Indian ricegrass
nodes.desc: A bunchgrass of sandy ground that Wikipedia says is eaten by elk, mule deer and others, and whose seeds feed many rodents and birds.

nodes.name: Lesser sunflower
nodes.desc: An annual sunflower of sandy, disturbed soil whose seeds suit seed-eating rodents.

nodes.name: Darkling beetle
nodes.desc: Eleodes beetles mostly eat plant and animal debris, scavenging at night. They spray a foul liquid, yet coyotes and owls still eat them.

nodes.name: Northern grasshopper
nodes.desc: Chews grasses and wildflowers in summer and feeds birds, mice and other small predators.

nodes.name: Deer mouse
nodes.desc: A common, widely recorded rodent that eats seeds and insects and is prey for snakes, hawks and coyotes.

nodes.name: Ord's kangaroo rat
nodes.desc: Mostly eats seeds and caches them in burrows in loose sand. Coyotes, owls, hawks and snakes prey on it.

nodes.name: Mule deer
nodes.desc: Browses shrubs and grazes grasses. Wikipedia says cougars hunt it at night in the montane woodlands.

nodes.name: Elk
nodes.desc: Visits the dunes from surrounding habitats and grazes grasses such as ricegrass. Cougars take it, and coyotes and ravens use carcasses.

nodes.name: Great Sand Dunes tiger beetle
nodes.desc: A predatory beetle found only on sparsely vegetated sand in this park. Its whole range lies inside the protected park.

nodes.name: Bullsnake
nodes.desc: A large constrictor of the drier woodlands and sand country that eats rodents such as kangaroo rats and deer mice.

nodes.name: Red-tailed hawk
nodes.desc: Wikipedia says raptors hunt mice and kangaroo rats over the sand sheet. Red-tailed hawks also take snakes.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: The most recorded bird near the park. Eats insects and small animals and scavenges carcasses.

nodes.name: Cougar
nodes.desc: Wikipedia says cougars hunt mule deer at night in the park's montane woodlands. Elk are also a large prey.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: Eats rodents, snakes, beetles and carcasses, and takes deer and elk. It hunts the sand sheet and woodlands.
